pairs.question: Cui vae? Cuius patri vae? Cui rixae? Cui foveae? Cui sine causa vulnera? Cui suffusio oculorum?
pairs.answer: Nonne his qui morantur in vino et student calicibus epotandis?
pairs.derivation: Verse 29 is a genuine series of interrogatives (cui/cuius), a riddle asking to whom woe, brawls, pits, gratuitous wounds, and bleary eyes belong. Verse 30 directly answers it (nonne his qui morantur in vino...). Scaffolding stripped: the inline verse numbers 29 and 30 and the CAPUT 23 header. First word capitalized and question marks supplied; nothing omitted from either utterance. The verse-30 answer is contiguous and complete to its full stop (end of verse). Other interrogatives in the book (e.g. 6:27-28, 8:1, 18:14, 20:9, 20:24, 30:4) are rhetorical questions with no answering statement following, and the numerical-saying riddles of chapter 30 (tria sunt..., quattuor sunt...) are declarative enumerations, not interrogatives, so all are dropped.
